title: 被 (bèi) in Chinese: The Passive Voice, HSK 3 Grammar
description: How to use 被 (bèi) for the passive in Chinese: the word order, leaving out the doer, why the verb needs an ending, negatives with 没有, and HSK 3 examples.
h1: How to Use 被 for the Passive
lede: 被 (bèi) makes a passive sentence: the person or thing that something happened to comes first, and the one who did it comes after 被. It is mostly used for things that went wrong or were unexpected, and it is a key grammar point of HSK 3.

paras: Receiver + 被 + doer + verb + something else.

Start with the thing the action happened to, then 被, then who did it, then the verb. 我的手机被弟弟用坏了 tells the same story as 弟弟把我的手机用坏了, but it starts from my phone and what happened to it, not from my brother.

examples.zh: 我的手机被弟弟用坏了。
examples.py: Wǒ de shǒujī bèi dìdi yònghuài le.
examples.en: My phone got broken by my little brother.
The cake was eaten by my little sister.

examples.py: Zhè jiàn shì bèi lǎoshī zhīdào le.
examples.en: The teacher found out about this.

paras: If you don't know or don't need to say who did it, put the verb straight after 被. To say "someone", use 被人.

examples.py: Wǒ de qiánbāo bèi rén názǒu le.
Nà běn shū bèi jièzǒu le.

examples.zh: 他的自行车被人骑走了。
examples.py: Tā de zìxíngchē bèi rén qízǒu le.
examples.en: Someone rode off on his bike.

sections.h2: The verb needs something after it
paras: As with 把, the verb in a 被 sentence can't stand alone. After it, add a result such as 坏 or 完, a direction such as 走 or 回家, or at least 了. 我的手机被弟弟用 is not a complete sentence.

English uses the passive far more often than Chinese. 被 is mostly for things that happened to someone or something and were bad, unwanted or unexpected. When it is obvious that the subject can't do the action itself, Chinese usually leaves 被 out: say 作业做完了, not 作业被做完了.

examples.py: Tā bèi māma jiào huí jiā le.

paras: To say something didn't happen, put 没有 before 被, not before the verb, and leave out 了. To warn someone, put 别 before 被. To ask who did it, put 谁 after 被.
In everyday speech, 让 can take the place of 被, but then you must say who did it.

examples.zh: 我的电脑没有被他用坏。
examples.py: Wǒ de diànnǎo méiyǒu bèi tā yònghuài.
Nǐ de shǒujī bèi shéi názǒu le?
Wǒ de dàngāo ràng dìdi chī le.
examples.en: My little brother ate my cake.

worksheet.title: 被 Passive Worksheet: HSK 3 Printable with Answers
worksheet.description: A free printable 被 (bèi) passive worksheet for HSK 3: 20 exercises (被 or 把, word order, fix the mistake) with an answer key.

exercises.instructions: Write 被 or 把 in each gap. The English tells you what the sentence means.

items.en: My little brother took my phone.
My little brother took my phone.
Close the door.
My little sister ate my bread.

items.zh: 他＿＿老师叫到办公室去了。
items.en: The teacher called him to the office.
Please put these things by the door.
Someone has borrowed that book.
Mum has washed the clothes.

exercises.instructions: Write the words as one correct sentence with 被.

items.en: The cat ate my fish.
Someone took his money.
The children didn't finish the cake.
answers: 那个蛋糕没有被孩子们吃完。

items.en: Who took your book?
The teacher saw us.
A friend has borrowed my umbrella.
answers: 我的雨伞被朋友借走了。

exercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Write the correct sentence.

items.en: My little brother took my cup away.
answers: 我的杯子被弟弟拿走了。

items.en: My little sister ate the apples.

items.zh: 我的钱被弟弟没有拿走。
items.en: My little brother didn't take my money.
answers: 我的钱没有被弟弟拿走。

items.en: He borrowed my book.
The teacher saw me.
My little brother ate my fruit.
